SubHub needs Android’s display-over-other-apps permission to show Popup Storm and its persistent stop control.
Enable Popup Storm and allow overlay access first.

Popup Storm spawns moving images at random screen positions, sometimes in quick bursts. If you have epilepsy, photosensitive seizures, migraines, or feel unwell from rapid visual changes, do not enable it.\n\nA persistent STOP STORM control remains above every popup. Android’s notification can also stop protection.
Setup, privacy, repairs, and feature guidance.
Required overlay and notification permissions are ready.

1. Choose your censor style and detector preset in Censor settings.
2. Tap Start Censoring.
3. Grant Android overlay access if requested.
4. Select a screen or app in Android’s capture prompt.
5. Stop from SubHub or its persistent notification.
Display over other apps lets SubHub place censor boxes above other apps. Screen recording uses Android’s capture prompt for each new session. App Mode needs Accessibility enabled once.

Protection analyzes frames locally with the imported ONNX model and stabilizes detections with object tracking. Whole-screen MediaProjection remains active for its current recording session. Android 11+ Accessibility App Mode is the persistent automatic path: enable it once, then SubHub can wake for all apps or selected launcher apps without another prompt on every app opening. Selected mode schedules no screenshots or inference after you leave a watched app. Protected apps may still block screenshots, and platform-secure windows cannot be bypassed.

The built-in browser provides tabs, bookmarks, accurately labeled private tabs, DOM pre-blur, ad filtering, search suggestions when enabled, full-screen media, and bounded downloads. Private tabs reduce retained local browser state, but Android WebView still shares a process-level cookie jar.

Export censors selected gallery images on device and saves new copies. Optional source deletion always requires a second confirmation and may trigger an additional Android provider prompt. Browser images can be downloaded normally or scanned and censored before saving.
Settings apply live. Profiles save named setups, packs add themes and phrases, and Commitment Pact seals configuration behind a keeper code and countdown.

Popup Storm can spawn moving images in rapid bursts. Read and accept the photosensitivity warning before enabling it. A separate STOP STORM control remains above every popup. Stopping the storm does not trap the device, disable Android controls, or prevent uninstalling SubHub.

Use Fix Next Permission above if censor overlays do not appear. Check Local Diagnostics for service state, active model/provider, frame rate, latency, and sanitized errors. If detection cannot start, re-import the licensed ONNX models. If accessibility capture stalls, disable and re-enable the service in Android settings.

Detection, tracking, app assignments, statistics, profiles, packs, diagnostics, and Wallet history stay on device. PayPal credentials entered in Dom Settings and saved-wallet IDs are encrypted for this installation; checkout and device risk data go directly to the selected PayPal environment. Browser traffic and optional search suggestions still contact the sites or provider you choose.
After restart, SubHub restores the last protection state. A sealed pact always re-arms App Mode when Android allows it. Screen recording still needs a new Android capture prompt.
